name: Guangzhou Baiyun International Airport
before:
The CAN code gives away its history: it comes from Canton, the old romanisation of Guangzhou, and the airport still carries it. Baiyun sits north of the city in Guangdong province and handles more passengers than any other airport in mainland China, with 63.1 million through its doors in 2023, putting it twelfth in the world that year. For a strange stretch in 2020, when much of global aviation stopped, it was briefly the busiest airport anywhere.

Most travellers passing through are connecting. It is the main hub for China Southern Airlines and also a base for Hainan Airlines, Shenzhen Airlines, 9 Air and FedEx Express, so freight moves through in serious volume alongside the passenger traffic. Cargo numbers put it second in China.

Terminal 2 has a five-star rating from Skytrax, with the airport as a whole rated four-star, which tells you the newer facilities are a step up. Five commercial runways operate here, a first in China, and the airport was also the country's first certified to 4F standard, meaning it takes the largest aircraft flying.
after:

It is a hub for China Southern Airlines, and freight moves through in serious volume alongside the passenger traffic. Cargo numbers put it second in mainland China.

Terminal 2 has a five-star rating from Skytrax, with the airport as a whole rated four-star. Five commercial runways operate here.

claims.why: Held back: the old text says nothing about which terminals are in use, so under the like-for-like rule this replaces nothing, though it is the change most likely to catch a traveller out. Terminal 3 and the fifth runway opened on 30 October 2025 (Xinhua, Guangzhou government, China Daily, South, Wikipedia). All eleven airlines left in Terminal 1 (Air China, Shenzhen Airlines, Hainan Airlines and eight more) moved to Terminal 3 from 2am on 7 May 2026, and Terminal 1 closed for renovation (South, Yangcheng Evening News, the Guangzhou Youth League, Wikipedia, which says its flights went to Terminal 2 or 3). The metro stops at Terminals 1 and 2 only, and the Terminal 1 station is now passed without stopping; for Terminal 3 the city's advice is Metro Line 3 to Gaozeng and a shuttle bus. The airport's own staff tell passengers to check their terminal with the airline. Was to read: "Terminal 3 opened on 30 October 2025, and since 7 May 2026 Terminal 1 has been closed for renovation, its airlines moved to Terminal 3, so check which terminal a flight uses."
